clue.text: Life of a celeb that's been shot?

definitions.text: Life of a celeb that's been shot?

parts.words: Life of a celeb that's been shot?
parts.note: reads like a famous person gunned down, but 'shot' is filming and 'life' is a life story put on screen

explanation.surface: A grim question about a celebrity who has been gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a shooting; here it means filmed, so the life of a celebrity that has been shot is a film of that life.
explanation.definitionFit: A film telling the story of a real person's life is a biographical picture, shortened in the trade.

clue.text: Prick causes football team to drop point

indicators.note: to drop says the compass letter is taken out of the team's name

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A football team losing a point is a wound to its pride.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURS is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; 'to drop' removes S (south, a compass point) to leave the verb for goad.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur a horse is to prick it with a spiked heel; both verbs mean to jab with a point.

clue.text: Grope — fellow snapped: "Led on!"

indicators.note: something snapped is broken, so the letters of the quoted words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man accused of groping hits back that he was led on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' looks like the fellow's angry reply, but it breaks up LED ON into ONDLE, placed after F.
explanation.definitionFit: To fondle someone is to caress or handle them, an unwanted grope being a crude version.

clue.text: Climax produced by adult muscles reportedly

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: reportedly says the muscles word is heard rather than written, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: pecs are the pectoral muscles of the chest

explanation.surface: A suggestive line about a climax brought on by a grown-up's muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: PECS (chest muscles) said out loud sounds like PEX, which follows A for adult.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the top or highest point, just as a climax is the peak of something.

clue.text: (&19dn.) Even less sensitive figure in PM's place?

parts.note: numb means without feeling, so more numb is even less sensitive
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A dig that the prime minister's seat holds someone even more unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'more numb', not as a count. Together with 19 the answer is Number Ten, 10 Downing Street, the official home of the UK prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten is shorthand for 10 Downing Street, the British prime minister's residence and office.

clue.text: Large body and arse concerning? Loosen up!

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a large international body
butt is slang for the backside
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A crude instruction to a big person to relax their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large body' suggests a fat person; it is the United Nations. 'Loosen up' is taken literally, undoing buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo the fastenings of a garment is literally to loosen it, so the command fits.

clue.text: Polish brewer with a bent for kinky gear?

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of brewer and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brewer from Poland with a taste for fetish clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but is the verb, giving RUB; 'bent' scrambles BREWER and A into BERWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex and rubber clothing are a staple of fetish dress, the kinky kind of outfit.

clue.text: US president: "Vital to crush news journalist!"

indicators.note: to crush says the vital word squeezes the next letters into its middle

parts.note: something vital is key, essential
N stands for new, and doubling a letter makes a plural, as pp is pages, so news gives NN
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A president's rallying cry that it is essential to suppress the press.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY is wrapped round NN (plural of N, new) and ED (editor), giving John F Kennedy, the 35th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: John F Kennedy was the thirty-fifth holder of the White House office, assassinated in 1963.

clue.text: Unprepared, one gets married — swift end of you?

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
prompt means quick, swift

indicators.note: end of says only the final letter of the word you is used

explanation.surface: Someone who weds without planning is asked if this is the quick end of their freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: I and M come first, then PROMPT, then U, the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off the cuff, without rehearsal or preparation, is extempore.

clue.text: Futile to apply common sense to English?

parts.note: nous is a word for common sense or gumption

explanation.surface: A sigh that there is no point using common sense on the English.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS followed by E reads as the two words NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort that achieves nothing is pointless, without any purpose or result.

clue.text: Republican party welcomes one in peace? That's absurd!

indicators.note: in places the Republican-party group inside the word for peace

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace

indicators.note: welcomes says the party letters take in the word for one

parts.note: a do is a party
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A Republican party claiming to welcome peace is presented as a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: R and DO take A inside to give RADO, which goes inside PAX.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory statement or situation, one that seems absurd, is called this.

clue.text: Royal house on the rocks after this?

explanation.surface: A question about which royal dynasty ends up on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' suggests a marriage in trouble; it is the barman's term for a drink poured over ice, and this American whiskey is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bourbons are the dynasty of French and Spanish kings; it is also the American corn whiskey often taken over ice.

clue.text: Ex-president accepting writer who could make up a cabinet

definitions.text: who could make up a cabinet

indicators.note: accepting says the president's name takes another word inside it

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president
a pen is a writer, the tool that writes

explanation.surface: A former president takes on a writer to form a government cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up a cabinet' looks like forming a government; it means building a cupboard. PEN goes inside CARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker who builds furniture such as a cupboard is a joiner by trade.

clue.text: Drills, tries to break concrete — shit at first

indicators.note: to break says the tries word splits the concrete word open

parts.note: concrete means real, actual
a judge hears or tries a case

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of shit is taken

explanation.surface: Workers practise breaking concrete, though the first try is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' is the court sense, HEARS, set inside REAL; the S at the end is the first letter of 'shit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drills are practice sessions, the run-throughs that prepare people for the real thing.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Those people: idiots, hoi polloi

parts.note: them means those people
asses are fools, idiots

explanation.surface: A snob writes off the common people as idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: THEM and ASSES join across 15 and 22 to make the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi, Greek for 'the many', means ordinary people, the general public.

clue.text: Ready for bed, went to bed … about to withdraw

indicators.note: to withdraw says the word for about is taken out of the bedtime word

parts.note: retired means went to bed
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone sleepy goes to bed, about to withdraw for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) is taken off RETIRED, and 'withdraw' also echoes another sense of retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepy and worn out is ready for sleep.

clue.text: Broadcaster, bore: "A way to access EU countries"

definitions.text: A way to access EU countries

parts.note: a TV channel is a broadcaster
a bore is a tunnel, a hole drilled through

explanation.surface: A broadcaster pompously describes the route to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is a tedious person on the surface; here it is a drilled passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail link under the sea between England and France connects Britain to mainland Europe.

clue.text: Name one part of a film featuring Conservative leader's birth

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: featuring says the film part takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a scene is a part of a film

indicators.note: leader's says only the first letter of Conservative is taken

explanation.surface: A film scene showing the birth of a Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: N and A come first, then SCENE with C, the first letter of 'Conservative', put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the coming into being of something, its origin or start.

clue.text: see 5dn.
Grim, sad Cameron on quitting: "stuffed by a bastard"

indicators.note: stuffed by says the remaining letters are filled with the last two pieces
sad means sorry or pitiful, so the letters are rearranged
quitting says the word on leaves the name

parts.note: B is a dictionary abbreviation for bastard

explanation.surface: A gloomy David Cameron, leaving office, is mocked by a heckler.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron loses ON to leave CAMER, which 'sad' rearranges to MACRE; A and B (bastard) go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something macabre is ghastly and gruesome, grim in its dwelling on death.

clue.text: Top grade state store

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams
Mass is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.surface: A state warehouse rated top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State store' looks like a government shop; 'store' is a verb, to collect.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather up and keep a supply of things is to accumulate it.

clue.text: An assorted group of males get on (with ire controlled)

parts.note: men are males
to get on is to grow older, to age

indicators.note: controlled says the letters of ire are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Men growing older are advised to keep their temper in check.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN and AGE are followed by RIE, the letters of 'ire' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed collection of people or things is likened to a zoo of wild animals.

clue.text: see 15dn.
Grand promenade: hazard

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an amble is a leisurely walk, a promenade

explanation.surface: A grand seafront walk turns out to be a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' is the verb, to risk, not a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard money or a guess is to risk or wager it.

clue.text: About to overturn foreign money commission

indicators.note: to overturn says the word for about is turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A deal on foreign currency is about to be reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE turned round gives ER, then RAND follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A task one is commissioned to do, a job or mission for someone else, is a run.

clue.text: Admittance about bullshit Conservative being ditched — it's painful

indicators.note: about says the shortened admittance word goes round the slang letters
being ditched says the abbreviation for Conservative is dropped

parts.note: access is admittance, a means of entry

explanation.surface: A complaint that Conservative nonsense about admittance hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: ACCESS loses one C to give ACESS, which goes round BS.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen pocket of pus under the skin is a sore, tender thing.

clue.text: Tripper's drinks holder

explanation.surface: A day-tripper is carrying something to hold drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripper's' means 'tripper is': someone who trips and falls is one. The ''s' is 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who falls over is one who takes a tumble; a flat-bottomed drinking glass also has this name.

clue.text: Silly mistake, being in party politics

indicators.note: being in says the letters sit inside the phrase party politics

explanation.surface: A gaffe made within party politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'parTY POlitics'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip in typing or printing is a small careless error.

clue.text: Express goes after "Liberal refuge"

indicators.note: goes after says the express word is placed behind the Liberal letter

parts.note: to air a view is to express it

explanation.surface: The Express newspaper pursues a Liberal sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the newspaper; it is the verb, to air. AIR comes after L.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is its hiding place, a retreat or shelter.

clue.text: Something unearthed from the past of facile right-winger rejected?

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dig at a glib right-winger's buried past.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'faCILE Right' gives the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An object surviving from an earlier age, dug up by archaeologists, is an artefact of history.

clue.text: Terrible lies upon suppressing vote — action Reform is often having to make?

definitions.text: action Reform is often having to make

indicators.note: suppressing says the rearranged letters hold the vote mark down inside them
terrible means awful, so the letters of lies upon are rearranged

parts.note: X is the mark made when voting

explanation.surface: Reform UK, telling dreadful lies and stifling votes, keeps having to throw people out.
explanation.walkthrough: LIES UPON rearranged holds X. Reform UK, the British right-wing party, has repeatedly had to throw out members.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing a member from a party is ejection, something Reform UK has done often.
